newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close weaker as banks lose ground.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close weaker as banks lose ground.

* Toronto stocks closed weaker on Monday, retreating from Friday's highs, as falling banks outweighed rising golds. * 82.2 million shares traded worth C$1.3 billion.
Toronto stocks closed lower on Monday, retreating from recent highs, as weaker banks and oils outweighed rising golds and investors took profits.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index lost 24.69 points to close at 6467.41. Trading was moderate at 82.3 million shares worth C$1.3 billion.

Earlier in the session, the index hit a new intra-session high of 6507.08 before being dampened by profit-taking in financial and energy issues. "These things can't be going up forever," said ScotiaMcLeod trading director Fred Ketchen.
Despite today's losses, Ketchen forecast Toronto would roll higher. "This market still has got a lot of legs to it."
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-groups ended higher, led by golds, consumer products and conglomerates. The weaker side included heavyweight oils, banks and transportation.
Declining issues beat out advancers 521 to 437, while 303 closed steady.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* The tumble in energy issues was led by Abacan Resources, after the Calgary-based oil firm said its cash flow in 1997 and 1998 would be much lower than analysts' forecasts.
Abacan lost 62 percent of its value, falling 5.03 to 3.07 on more than 11 million shares.
* Floor and wallcovering maker Domco Inc soared after a takeover offer by U.S.-based Armstrong World Industries Inc. Domco rose 5.25 to 20.

Armstrong World Industries Inc said on Monday that it offered to buy its Canadian rival for C$23 a share or C$488 million. It also said that it launched a lawsuit to prevent France's Sommer Allibert SA from merging its business, including 57 percent- owned Domco, with Germany's Tarkett AG.
* Ault Foods Ltd jumped 2.20 to 34.20.

Its board said on Monday that it agreed to a C$34 a share or C$415 million white knight takeover bid by Parmalat Finanziaria SPA. Rival Saputo Group, which has bid C$28 a share, did not rule out a higher bid.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
